task_description: Designing novel alloy electrocatalyst surface structures with high activity and selectivity for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), specifically by optimizing for near-optimal CO adsorption energy (ΔECO ≈ −0.67 eV) while simultaneously satisfying constraints on hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) suppression (ΔEH + 0.27 ≥ 0.6 eV) and thermodynamic stability (formation energy < −0.1 eV/atom).

datasets.db_description: A database of catalyst surfaces created by Tran et al., containing diverse surface structures used to pretrain both the CDVAE generative model and the supervised DimeNet++ property prediction models in this work; it provides the structural foundation for generating new alloy surfaces and serves as the training data for predicting CO adsorption energy (ΔECO), H adsorption energy (ΔEH), and formation energy (Ef) — all critical for guiding inverse design toward CO2RR-active, HER-suppressing, and stable alloys.

The Open Quantum Materials Database, used to train the MEGNet model for predicting formation energy (Ef); this enables rapid, high-accuracy thermodynamic stability assessment of generated alloy surfaces without costly DFT calculations, supporting the third selection criterion (Ef < −0.1 eV/atom) during screening of CO2RR candidates.

A curated dataset of 110 DFT-validated alloy surface structures selected from the 250,000 MAGECS-generated candidates, containing DFT-calculated |ΔECO + 0.67| and ΔEH values; it is used to benchmark and validate the performance of the ML property predictors (DimeNet++ and MEGNet) and to support experimental prioritization — directly enabling the final step of identifying synthesizable, high-performing CO2RR electrocatalysts.
